ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
 
 Ind. Code ch . 8-1-26 provides t he procedure for the Indiana Utility Regulatory 
Commission’s Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”) to find violations of said chapter. Upon 
review of those findings, the Indiana Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee 
(“Advisory Committee”) reviews those recommendations and recommends civil penalties in the 
Case.   
 
The Cases received pursuant to Ind . Code ch. 8-1-26 and ripe for Commission action are 
attached hereto and collectively referred to as the Advisory Committee Recommendations.  
 
Pursuant to statute, the Advisory Committee has submitted their recommendations to the 
Commission. The Commission UPHOLDS the findings of violations by the Pipeline Safety 
Division and APPROVES the recommendations of the Advisory Committee as listed on the 
attached pages. The Assistant General Counsel to the Division is directed to prepare and send 
notice to the parties advising them of the determination. 
 
Any approved civil penalties are due within 90 days of the date of this Order unless 
payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission.   
 
Any approved trainings must be completed no later than 180 days from the date of this 
Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due.   
 
IT IS SO ORDERED. 
 
HUSTON, FREEMAN, KREVDA, AND OBER CONCUR; ZIEGNER ABSENT: 
 
APPROVED: 
 
I hereby certify that the above is a true 
and correct copy of the Order as approved.

cat > $TMPDIR/a.py <<'E'
import re,glob,collections
c=collections.Counter();tot=0;nocity=0;pages=0
for f in glob.glob('/tmp/r2run-n9gtiaxm/data/text/*.txt'):
    for p in re.split(r'=== page \d+\n',open(f).read()):
        m=re.search(r'Damage Location:(.*?)The IURC',p,re.S)
        if not m: continue
        pages+=1
        body=m.group(1)
        first=body.split('\n')[0].strip()
        lines=[l.strip() for l in body.split('\n') if l.strip()]
        if not first: lines=lines[5:]
        loc=' '.join(lines)
        if ',' not in loc: nocity+=1;continue
        city=loc.rsplit(',',1)[1].strip().lower()
        if not city: nocity+=1;continue
        c[city]+=1;tot+=1
print(pages,tot,nocity)
t=c.most_common(8);print(t)
print(sum(v for k,v in t[:5]),sum(v for k,v in t[:5])/tot*100)
E
python3 -I $TMPDIR/a.py

content.text:
**Indianapolis** has the most cases, with **1,153**.

The five most common cities together account for **26.2%** of the cases that have a city. That is 2,606 of 9,942 cases.

| Rank | City | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | indianapolis | 1,153 |
| 2 | fort wayne | 529 |
| 3 | evansville | 445 |
| 4 | south bend | 295 |
| 5 | bloomington | 184 |

I parsed 9,953 cases from the 58 order text files. 11 had no comma or an empty city and were left out, which leaves the 9,942 above.

Some pages had the form labels and values split into separate blocks, so I re-paired them by position. Locations that wrapped onto a second line were joined before taking the text after the last comma. I did not check these by hand, so a few misread locations are possible. They would shift the counts slightly.
